systematic_read.airway_lungs: CURRENT: Trachea roughly midline as far as rotation allows. A thin vertical linear density projects over the tracheal air column; an endotracheal tube is possible but not confirmed. Low lung volumes. Bilateral hazy and reticular opacity, most marked in the perihilar and mid zones and extending to the lower zones. Hazy opacity at the right base with an indistinct right hemidiaphragm. Left base and retrocardiac region are dense, and the left hemidiaphragm is obscured. No pleural line seen to suggest pneumothorax, but supine films are insensitive for this. PRIOR: Trachea roughly midline. Lungs well inflated. Lung markings are within normal limits or slightly prominent in the right perihilar and lower zone. No focal consolidation or discrete nodule seen. No pneumothorax seen.

Hila are not clearly enlarged; the right hilum is partly overlapped by the lead coil.

findings.description: Hazy and reticular opacity in the right perihilar and mid zone, extending to the upper and lower zones, on the current film. The prior shows at most slightly prominent right perihilar markings.
findings.evidence: Markings are denser and less distinct on the current than on the prior, and the change reaches the mid and upper zones, where low volumes alone have less effect. The current is AP supine with low volumes, which crowds markings and redistributes vessels, so technique may explain part of it. The pattern is bilateral; interstitial or alveolar fluid is one consideration.

findings.description: Hazy and reticular opacity in the left perihilar and mid zone on the current film. The prior left lung looks clear where it is not covered by the generator.
findings.evidence: Left perihilar and mid zone markings are denser and less distinct than on the prior, matching the right side. The AP supine low-volume technique and the overlying generator limit the comparison.

findings.description: Hazy opacity at the right base with an indistinct medial right hemidiaphragm on the current film. The right base and dome are clear and sharp on the prior.
findings.evidence: The right dome is sharp on the prior and partly lost on the current. Low volumes and supine position crowd the base and can mimic basal opacity. Atelectasis, layering pleural fluid and airspace opacity cannot be told apart on this film.

findings.description: Dense left lower zone and retrocardiac opacity with loss of the left hemidiaphragm outline on the current film. The left dome is visible on the prior.
findings.evidence: The left dome and lower left heart border are obscured on the current and visible on the prior. Low volumes, AP magnification of the heart and supine layering of fluid could each produce this. Collapse or consolidation of the left lower zone, pleural fluid, or both, are possible.

findings.description: Left costophrenic angle is obscured on the current film, with graded haze over the left lower zone. No definite blunting on the prior.
findings.evidence: The left angle is not definable on the current. Supine position layers fluid posteriorly, so the presence and amount of effusion cannot be compared with an upright PA prior.

findings.evidence: Generator and coil-bearing leads are seen in a similar overall layout on both films. No gross lead discontinuity seen. Exact lead tip positions cannot be compared between PA and AP supine projections.

response.limits: This is a blind first read without indication or dates. The comparison is limited: the prior is PA with adequate inspiration, and the current is AP supine portable with low lung volumes. No size change is reported for the heart or any lesion because the projection differs. The lung and pleural changes are marked indeterminate because technique could account for some or all of the difference; they are flagged time-sensitive for early review. Device generator, leads and external monitoring wires hide parts of the left lung and mediastinum. Rotation is hard to judge on both films. The images are downsampled, so fine detail is unreliable, including small nodules, lead integrity and tube tips. No measurements are given; the radiologist measures in PACS. This draft is for resident and attending review.
